name: MN-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 partisan lean in a Twin Cities suburban district
Long-serving incumbent Betty McCollum with a large fundraising edge
Challenger Paul Wikstrom raised only ~$28k with minimal cash
model.rationale: The D+18 lean, McCollum's incumbency and roughly 45-to-1 fundraising advantage over Wikstrom, and markets pricing her near 96% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold. No polls or expert ratings exist, so uncertainty stays moderately wide, but nothing suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing McCollum under 60% or significant outside spending against her would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Betty McCollum, a long-serving Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this St. Paul-area district that leans Democratic by 18 points. She has raised about $1.25 million and holds nearly $500,000 in cash, while Republican Paul Wikstrom has raised under $30,000 with almost nothing banked and no outside support on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets price McCollum's chances around 96%. With the incumbent renominated and no signs of a serious challenge, the seat is expected to remain safely Democratic in November.
